extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent owners and practitioners handling ex parte and third‑party requested reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for handling submissions, service, defective/untimely papers, petitions to revive, final actions, panel review, and post‑final practice in U.S. reexamination proceedings (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service requirement in third‑party requested reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: After the filing of a request for reexamination by a third party requester, any document filed by either the patent owner or the third party requester must be served on the other party (or parties where proceedings are merged) in the manner provided in 37 CFR 1.248.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A certificate of service must be provided to the Office within a shortened statutory period of ONE MONTH or THIRTY DAYS, whichever is longer, from the mailing date of the notice of lack of service; failure to timely make service may result in denial of consideration. Form paragraph 22.15 may be used to give notice. If the submission lacking proof of service is a response to a final rejection, do not use PTOL‑475 or form paragraph 22.15; instead issue PTOL‑467/PTOL‑467A explaining the lack of proof of service and continue to apply the time period set in the final rejection (extended by two months if first response after final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to serve required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party fails to serve the required submission in response to notice, the submission may be refused consideration by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific consequences: (A) For a patent owner statement or a third party reply, the submission may be refused consideration and, if refused, will not be addressed other than to inform parties of the lack of consideration; (B) For a patent owner response to an Office action, the response may be refused consideration and prosecution may be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(d) unless the patent owner otherwise completely responded to the Office action. See related MPEP sections for details (e.g., §§ 2220, 2249, 2251, 2266).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expunging inappropriate or unauthorized papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed during reexamination that are inappropriate (unauthorized or improper) will be expunged from the official file by marking them 'closed' and 'non‑public'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inappropriate paper has already been scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW), it cannot be physically returned but will be marked non‑public/closed so it does not appear in the active public IFW record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Premature patent owner response (expungement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the patent owner is NOT the requester, any response or amendment filed by owner prior to an order to reexamine is premature and will not be considered and will be expunged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper submitted on behalf of a third party (expungement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission filed on behalf of a third party will not be considered and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where third party paper is submitted as part of a patent owner response, see MPEP §§ 2254 and 2266 for guidance on handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on iterative oppositions/rebuttals
rubrics_metrics.description: If an opposition to a patent owner petition is filed by a third party requester (or vice versa), any further paper in opposition/rebuttal/response to that opposition will not be considered and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There must be a limitation on party iterations of input given the statutory mandate for special dispatch in reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: No patent owner statement — requester replies inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent owner fails to file a statement within the prescribed limit, any reply by the requester is inappropriate, will not be considered, and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference to § 1.535 procedure and timing; ensures requester participation ends if owner does not act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late response by requester (two‑month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any response by the requester submitted more than two months from the date of service of the patent owner's statement will not be considered and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict two‑month window applies to requester replies following service of the patent owner statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requester participation ends after authorized reply
rubrics_metrics.description: The active participation of the reexamination requester ends with the reply pursuant to § 1.535; any further submission on behalf of the requester will not be considered and will be expunged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions for extension of time by requester or other attempts to continue participation are inappropriate and will be expunged because the requester lacks continuing participation rights in the reexamination proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party submissions generally destroyed or expunged
rubrics_metrics.description: A third‑party submission will be destroyed or expunged unless it raises only issues appropriate under 37 CFR 1.501 or consists solely of a prior decision on the patent by another forum (e.g., a court) or presentation of a paper of record in litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2207, 2286, 2282 for examples. Submissions raising other matters outside 1.501 are not entered into the patent file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention of defective papers in file — unsigned papers (owner)
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by owner which are unsigned or signed by fewer than all of the owners (no attorney of record or acting in representative capacity) are identified as defective and will be retained in the reexamination file (with appropriate handling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include 37 CFR § 1.33 and related provisions; such papers are noted in the file rather than simply returned when expungement is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proof of service — retention or denial of consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by the patent owner (or requester) that lack required proof of service on the other party may be denied consideration; some defective papers are nonetheless retained in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Owner papers lacking proof of service may be denied consideration; requester papers lacking proof of service may also be denied. See 37 CFR §§ 1.248, 1.530(b), 1.510(b)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely papers by owner — not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: If the owner files a paper after the period set for response (i.e., untimely), the paper will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely owner submissions are treated as defective and not considered; timing rules are strict in reexamination to preserve special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsigned or defective requester papers — not considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed by requester which are unsigned will not be considered; requester papers lacking proof of service where required may be denied consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference: 37 CFR §§ 1.510(b)(5), 1.33, 1.248. Signatures and proof of service are essential for requester filings to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third‑party citations filed after reexamination order delayed from patent file
rubrics_metrics.description: Citations by third parties based solely on prior art patents or publications filed after the date of the order to reexamine are not entered into the patent file but are delayed until the reexamination proceedings have been concluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2206; ensures the patent file is not updated prematurely with post‑order third‑party art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's authority to revive reexamination/proceedings (revival/petition)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish procedures (including fee requirements) to revive an unintentionally abandoned application, accept an unintentionally delayed response by the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding, or accept other unintentionally delayed actions upon petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revival fees are specified (e.g., $1,700 for multiple revival petitions under 35 U.S.C. 41(a)(7)); Director may refund part of the fee in exceptional circumstances; petitions for revival are decided in the Office of Patent Legal Administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.137 petition requirements for unintentional delay
rubrics_metrics.description: A grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.137 must be accompanied by: (1) The reply required to the outstanding Office action or notice (unless previously filed); (2) the petition fee as set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(m); (3) any terminal disclaimer and fee if required; and (4) a statement that the entire delay in filing the required reply was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information where there is a question about whether the delay was unintentional. Requests for reconsideration of a denial must be filed within two months and may be extended only under 37 CFR 1.550(c) (not § 1.136). See MPEP § 711.03(c) for more details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unavoidable‑delay petitions eliminated — only unintentional standard applies
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions based on 'unavoidable delay' are no longer available; 37 CFR 1.137 was amended to eliminate the unavoidable standard and to provide revival only for unintentional delay, implementing the PLTIA changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change applies to applications and reexamination proceedings regardless of filing/ordering dates (effective December 18, 2013). Historical case law context (e.g., Aristocrat) is noted for background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration (renewed petition) timing and form
rubrics_metrics.description: Reconsideration of a decision dismissing or denying a 37 CFR 1.137 petition must be requested within two months from the mail date of the decision; the submission should include a cover letter entitled 'Renewed Petition under 37 CFR 1.137'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time for reconsideration are only available under 37 CFR 1.550(c); extensions under 37 CFR 1.136 are not available in reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for issuing a final Office action in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Before issuing a final action, a clear issue should be developed between the examiner and the patent owner, and the examiner should generally provide the patent owner twice with information and references useful in defining the Office's position on unpatentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision ordering reexamination will identify substantial new questions of patentability. The first Office action should reflect consideration of request arguments, owner statements, and requester replies and apply all relevant grounds of rejection. The second Office action generally will be made final (criteria analogous to MPEP § 706.07(a)). Final rejections should carefully review and reiterate all outstanding grounds and rebut patent owner arguments so the owner can judge advisability of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraphs and content for final actions (¶ 22.09, ¶ 22.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rejection letters in reexamination should conclude with form paragraph 22.09 ('THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL') or 22.10 ('THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL, NECESSITATED BY AMENDMENT'), with appropriate brackets filled in for response periods or amendment dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify the shortened statutory period (normally two months). Explain that extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not apply; extensions are provided under 37 CFR 1.550(c) with strict filing and fee requirements and are granted only for sufficient cause and reasonable time. Filing a timely first response to a final rejection is construed as a request to extend by two months but the statutory period cannot exceed six months from the mailing date of the final action. Final Office actions must be signed by a primary examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments submitted with a request filed under 35 U.S.C. 302, or after reexamination is ordered and which comply with 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j), will generally be entered for purposes of reexamination if submitted prior to a final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'new matter' amendment to the disclosure (35 U.S.C. 132) will be canceled and claims containing new matter will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112. New matter to drawings is ordinarily not entered. Where an amendment enlarges claim scope, the amendment will be entered but the appropriate claims will be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 305. See MPEP §§ 2234, 2250, 608.04.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review requirement for Office actions (§ 2271.01)
rubrics_metrics.description: A panel review will be conducted at each stage of the examiner’s examination in an ex parte reexamination proceeding for each Office action (except notices of informality/incomplete responses and matters outside examiner jurisdiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel makeup: three or more members including a manager and the examiner in charge; conferees should be primary examiners knowledgeable in the technology and mostly not involved in the original examination. Panel process: examiner informs manager, manager convenes panel, if conference confirms preliminary decision to reject/allow, the action is issued and signed by examiner with conferees initialing; if not confirmed, examiner reevaluates. Failure to hold conference must be challenged within two weeks of receipt of the Office action; failure alone is not grounds to vacate Office decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signatory authority for final Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: As with all other Office correspondence on the merits in a reexamination proceeding, the final Office action must be signed by a primary examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signature and conferees' initials are present to show panel review participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: After‑final practice and limitations on further prosecution
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a final rejection (that is not premature) has been entered in a reexamination proceeding, the patent owner no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution; consideration of amendments after final is governed by strict standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final and prior to or with appeal are governed by 37 CFR 1.116; amendments after appeal governed by 37 CFR 41.33. Patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.181 (within the time for filing a notice of appeal) to request withdrawal of the final rejection or entry of an amendment, but filing a petition under § 1.181 does not toll the time for filing a notice of appeal. Patent owner and examiner should identify and develop all issues (including evidence under 37 CFR 1.131(a) or 1.132) prior to the final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art cited by patent owner in prosecution can support a final action
rubrics_metrics.description: Where art is submitted in a prior art citation (e.g., IDS) and not accompanied by a statement similar to 37 CFR 1.97(e), the examiner may use the submitted art and make the next Office action final whether or not claims were amended, provided no other new ground of rejection is introduced based on the new art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a) and § 2206; absence of required statement may permit immediate reliance on owner‑submitted art to make an Office action final.
